analysis.title: markets / macro (Tony Pasquariello, 14 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Pasquariello sees a positive skew in the balance of risks through year-end 2026 and says the primary trend in the S&P 500 remains higher. His reasons are supportive near-term flows after position cleansing, seasonals after the midterms, continued AI demand, and nominal US GDP growth running above trend and accelerating in H2.

He expects 2027 to be more complicated. He expects more volatility and less upward convexity, which points to lower risk-adjusted returns, and describes a 'seesaw' of powerful countervailing forces that grinds out more modest gains.

Index performance diverged from how the market felt this week. A bellwether stock of the AI era lost over $500bn of market cap and the US 2-year note yield rose 33 bps on inflation concerns, yet NDX rallied 3.5%. Equal-weight S&P closed Friday's prior session about 1% from its all-time high.

Daily rotations in H2 2026 have been 'brutal' for leveraged participants, both professional and retail. The desk says separating signal from noise is unusually hard because of the volume of information.

Seasonal data: since 1952 the last seven weeks of the year have been up in 69% of occurrences, with an average rally of 2.1%. Pasquariello says the midterms being over puts the market in one of the best vol-adjusted periods of the year.

Positioning: since early October the trading community has liquidated a large amount of risk, in both net and gross exposure. Last week the GS franchise saw its biggest sale of global AI stocks in four years. Net exposure across the GS prime brokerage book is in the 3rd percentile of the past year.
Corporate supply versus demand (buybacks versus issuance) should improve meaningfully as November progresses.
AI demand: this week's volatility in AI infrastructure stocks also produced fresh evidence that AI demand remains 'insatiable', citing TSMC and CRWV.

2027 risks: the AI infrastructure buildout was larger than expected and uninterrupted for four years. The market has priced the scale, and the lack of interruption is increasingly at risk from US politicians. Regulation and tax increases are also possible.

Inflation: core inflation is sticky, and the latest CPI report suggests it is broadening. Pasquariello notes that bull markets typically end because the central bank removes liquidity, not from old age.
Supply: 2027 will likely see the largest increase in net supply (equity) since 2000, referenced to exhibits 6 and 14 in a linked piece.
Counterpoint: NDX is trending to be up in 17 of the past 18 years on total return, and sturdy GDP growth supports earnings growth and the broad bull uptrend.
The desk received many responses about the prior week's mention of concerns over the US credit market. Most were significantly negative.

Pasquariello says the US economy has never been more sensitive to the stock market's performance. He applies the Dow Theory 'primary trend is higher' to the S&P chart, and says Q2 2026 was something of a mini bubble.

sector_views.rationale: This week's volatility in AI infrastructure stocks came with fresh evidence of strong AI demand (TSMC, CRWV). Risk to the buildout's uninterrupted path rises in 2027 from US political action.

earnings_insights: Sturdy nominal GDP growth is cited as supportive of healthy earnings growth. No company-specific figures are given.

tension_points.bull_case: Positive skew through year-end 2026: supportive flows after position cleansing, strong seasonals (up 69% of years since 1952, average +2.1%), insatiable AI demand, and above-trend nominal GDP growth.
tension_points.bear_case: 2027 is more complicated: political risk to the AI buildout, more regulation and taxes, sticky and broadening core inflation, and the largest net supply increase since 2000, leading to more volatility and lower risk-adjusted returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Central bank removal of liquidity driven by broadening core inflation, which the note says is what ends bull markets.
